messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER: high error-rate detected on /v1/generate (5xx/timeouts). Alert rule: generate_api.rolling_error_rate > 10% for 5m. Paging on-call (maria).

maria: I'm on it. seeing alert in the dashboard — error rate ~18% and latency 95p creeping up. start time ~1845125400 per metrics.

jason: any obvious recent deploys? I don't see a generate service deploy in the last 2 hours.

lee: not me. infra deploys were earlier. i'll pull logs from scheduler and batching services.

maria: customer impact? are webhooks failing or just internal retries?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1845127890. Severity: P1. Channels: #incidents, #eng-oncall. Paging: maria -> jason.

jason: top-level snapshot:
- api gateway 5xx spike at ingress gateways (nginx) ~18%
- request timeouts concentrated on requests routed to model-group:gauss-xl and model-group:gauss-xl-quant
- queue depth on scheduler: 420 (usual <40)
- batching/scheduler CPU at 92% on several pods

maria: that queue depth screams head-of-line blocking. if one worker stalls it stacks up.

lee: grabbing scheduler logs:
```
2026-03-14T15:18:04Z scheduler-3 ERROR kvcache: stall detected, inflight=204 backlog=376
2026-03-14T15:18:12Z scheduler-3 WARN batcher: batch assemble timeout exceeded for 12s
2026-03-14T15:18:23Z scheduler-2 ERROR dispatch: downstream timeout to runtime (context deadline)
```

emily: also seeing increased zapped connections to runtime VMs (gpus). some pods show 5xx N/A on health checks.

maria: quick mitigation options: 1) enable overflow routing to smaller/compatible model variant 2) scale up scheduler workers 3) drain problematic runtime nodes 4) reduce max_batch_size to lower queueing latency. Which should we attempt first?

jason: do overflow routing first to reduce load hitting the saturated model. then scale scheduler (fast).

lee: I can flip overflow in the routing policy. patch:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/production
- match: model: gauss-xl
+ match: model: gauss-xl
  action: primary
+ fallback: gauss-medium (max_rate: 30%)
```
Applying now.

infra-bot: routing change applied by lee at 2026-03-14T15:21:07Z — fallback enabled to gauss-medium (30% max).

maria: monitoring now.

(2m pass)

emily: error rate dropped from 18% -> 12% within 120s, p95 latency improved slightly. queue depth down to 210.

jason: go ahead and scale scheduler replicas and bump worker threads. I'll run an emergency horizontal pod autoscaler override.

jason: command:
```
kubectl scale deployment scheduler --replicas=8 -n redwood-inference
kubectl patch hpa scheduler -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}' -n redwood-inference
```

infra-bot: scheduler scaled to 8 replicas. HPA minReplicas set to 6.

lee: also reducing max_batch_size to 64 to reduce batching latency temporarily.

lee: config set applied: max_batch_size=64; batching-window-ms=12

sre-bot: note: reducing batch size will increase token cost temporarily.

maria: good. watch customer impact and take notes for postmortem. who owns notifying customers if SLA is breached?

emily: I have a support thread open for the top 5 accounts with highest error volume. i'll send an interim status message: "We're mitigating increased errors, routing to fallback models. Expect degraded throughput; no data loss." anyone want to add?

jason: add ETA for full recovery 30-60m and link to metrics dash.

maria: metrics now look better: error rate 6%, queue depth 90, scheduler CPU ~55%. gateway 5xx back to baseline ~1.5%.

maria: initiating controlled restart of the two scheduler pods that reported the stall to clear stuck goroutines.

lee: command:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/scheduler -n redwood-inference --field-selector metadata.name=scheduler-2,metadata.name=scheduler-3
```

infra-bot: restart requested. pods terminating and recreate.

(rolling restart ~3m)

jason: restart successful. logs show no more 'stall detected' messages. queue drained to ~12.

emily: customer impact log:
- impacted customers: 12 (transient failures, retries succeeded for most)
- error types: 504 gateway timeouts, 502 runtime 5xx
- duration of elevated error window: ~35 minutes peak, mitigation reduced within 8 minutes after routing + scale
- severity: P1; no data loss reported; some SLA latency breaches for 5 customers

maria: great. capture these as part of incident notes. immediate actions list:
- follow-up: investigate root cause of runtime stalls (possible kernel OOM or network flake) -> assigned: infra team (jason)
- follow-up: evaluate batching defaults and safer auto-fallback thresholds -> assigned: eng-runtime (lee)
- follow-up: refine alert thresholds to include queue-depth-derived paging -> assigned: sre (maria)
- customer comms follow-up -> assigned: support (emily)

jason: early hypothesis: a subset of runtime hosts hit GPU driver stalls after long-lived KV cache growth. grabbing dmesg and containerOOM logs now.

lee: also will add additional metrics for per-runtime connection churn and KV cache size by host.

maria: marking incident as degraded->mitigated. leaving thread open for root cause and postmortem. if anything regresses, re-pager.

sre-bot: INC-2026-1845127890 status changed: mitigated. Actions recorded.

emily: I'll draft a short interim customer note and attach incident metrics. ETA for full postmortem: 48 hours.

maria: thanks everyone. quick retrospective note: fallback routing + scale was effective; need playbook step for automatic overflow when queue_depth > 200 for >2m.

jason: agreed. i'll own the automation ticket.

lee: logging ticket for batching defaults and safer quick-fallbacks.

maria: closing handoff to on-call for tomorrow's shift. last check: metrics stable. last_message_ts=1845128730 \n
